title: Person Registry — Pass A verdicts
description: What the registry pass's FIRST LLM call returns (#550, W9r): the whole cast, consolidated. Every unit person_registry.py's --prep emitted must appear exactly once across people[].units, non_person_forms[] and refusals[] -- that coverage is checked procedurally by --build's gate P3, not here, because JSON Schema cannot compare a document against a separate input file. NO COUNT FIELD EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THIS SCHEMA, deliberately: every count in the emitted registry is recomputed from disk by --build, so there is no field a model could assert one into. (The one integer the schema does allow is locator.footnote_n, which is a container ADDRESS resolved against the manifest, not a quantity.) Nothing in this document is trusted on its own -- each person, each identity_status with its reason, each typed claim and each printed surface becomes an isolated claim in registry_claims.json and must be affirmed by the SECOND, freshly-dispatched adjudication call before it reaches the artifact. This schema lives under assets/schemas/registry/ rather than assets/schemas/ on purpose: SKILL.md's Step 0a copy pass globs assets/schemas/*.json (non-recursive) and resume_setup.py's _schemas_dir_hash globs {durable_root}/schemas/*.schema.json (non-recursive), so a registry schema placed here changes no project's input_digest.

input_sha256.description: Copied verbatim from registry_input.json's own input_sha256. --build recomputes it from the prep document on disk and refuses a mismatch, so a verdict left behind by an earlier run over a different canon can never be consumed against the current one.

non_person_forms.description: Units judged not to denote a person. `category` is optional on a canon entry and absent on most, so person-vs-place-vs-work is a judgement made here, never read off the canon.

refusals.description: Units whose referent could not be settled. A refusal is the SAFE outcome and must be recorded rather than resolved by a guess -- two records for one man is untidy, one record for two men is wrong.

unit.description: The pass's unit of identity: a canon source_form, plus a canon_senses.json sense_id when the form is an adjudicated homonym split. sense_id is null for a canon entry and for a review_queue candidate. Never the bare spelling on its own -- one spelling can denote several people by construction in a naming system that fixes identity by patronymic or place.

locator.description: Where a quote is to be verified. Origin-aware because the three origins live in three different containers: a block's own plain_text, a verse.store[] entry's plain_text (the parent block carries only the placeholder), or a footnote definition block's plain_text.

quote.description: A span copied VERBATIM out of the container the locator names. --build re-reads that container from manifest.json and refuses a quote that is not a substring of it. That check proves the sentence exists; whether it STATES this claim is the adjudication pass's job, never this one's.

person_id.description: Unique within this document; the key relations use to point at each other. Restricted to a path-safe shape because it is echoed into the emitted registry and into PEOPLE.md.

units.description: Every unit this record claims. Two or more units is a merge -- an assertion that these forms denote one and the same person -- and one unit is still an assertion that this form denotes a person at all. Both are adjudicated by the same person claim.

identity_status.description: A fact about the IDENTITY, never about how often the person is mentioned -- mention_count is computed separately and carries that. BOTH values are adjudicated, together with identity_status_reason: "confirmed" asserts the identity is not contested, and "contested" is the safe status but its stated reason still reaches the reader -- and a reason about SCARCITY ("only one mention") is precisely the conflation this field exists to prevent. An unaffirmed status lands on "contested" with a deterministic reason; the adjudicator's own wording is kept in refuted_claims[].

printed_surfaces.description: Candidate target-language renderings as the book actually prints them -- strings only. A translator may inflect or decline a canonical form, so this is a judgement about the delivered text, not a copy of canonical_target_form (which --build counts anyway, for every unit, without being asked).

type.description: A closed vocabulary. No inverse of any of these is ever derived: an importer can invert a stated edge itself, and a plugin that derived them would be manufacturing relations the book did not state.

to_unregistered.description: The other party as the prose names them, when the book states a relation to somebody outside this project's cast. A real edge, not a defect -- so it is kept rather than dropped.

value.description: As the book states it, verbatim in whatever calendar and precision it uses -- never normalized to an ISO date, which would be an interpretation the quote does not support.
